messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT detected 2026-03-17T22:13:07Z — sev3: KV-cache / paged-attn slow warmup memory growth on gw-inference-usw2. Paging oncall: @maya @sam. Runbook: https://intra/runbooks/kv-warmup-slow-burn
maya: seeing repeated OOMs on model-serving pods (model: redwood-13b). Crash logs show CUDA allocation failures: `cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory` and container restart loops.
sam: stack shows lots of small allocations not reclaimed; paged-attn allocator resident pages growing ~3%/hr on some nodes. `attn_paged_alloc: failed to allocate page: out of memory` repeated.
juan: customer impact check — ACME-Pay traces show tail latency spikes +500ms and ~5% transient 503s for their inference route since ~21:50 PST. Zoe-cs pinged them and they're asking for ETA.
liam: I can take node work — marking suspected node ip-10-0-5-12 as suspect (high RSS).
maya: ops-bot, can you post current pod restart counts and OOM events?
ops-bot: pod restarts (last 15m): model-serving-0: 4, model-serving-1: 7, model-serving-2: 1. OOMs: 12. Node ip-10-0-5-12: 7 container restarts, 2 kernel OOMs.
liam: cordoning ip-10-0-5-12 now and draining non-critical pods. `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-12 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-5-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
sam: good. Also triggering an on-the-fly eviction threshold change to reduce resident set: `kubectl set env deployment/model-serving KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.65 -n prod` — will roll gradually.
maya: also toggled `KVCACHE_WARMUP_PREFETCH=false` on canary group to stop aggressive prefetch causing growth. Command: ```kubectl set env deployment/model-serving KVCACHE_WARMUP_PREFETCH=false -n prod```
juan: started a canary rolling restart on 3 pods (group 1). 1/3 done, 0 OOMs on restarted pod so far.
ops-bot: alert: node ip-10-0-5-12 flapped at 22:18:30 UTC; kubelet restarted.
maya: running compaction script on drained node snapshot: `/opt/internal/scripts/kv_compact.sh --force --limit=200` — frees page fragments and should reduce allocation churn.
sam: added temporary runtime flag to enable eager prune: `KVCACHE_EAGER_PRUNE=true` on model-serving deployment canary. This should aggressively evict cold entries to stop slow bleed.
liam: after cordon/drain, redistributed pods to healthier nodes. Monitoring for OOMs.
zoe-cs: ACME-Pay updated: they see reduced errors but still elevated latency. Asking for ETA and mitigation notes to share.
maya: quick customer note: we throttled warmup + increased eviction; we're doing rolling restarts, compaction, and node remediation. ETA for stabilization ~30–45m, follow up if regressions.
sam: snippet from `dmesg` on flapped node: `Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (model-server) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:98765kB, file-rss:1234kB` — fragmentation pattern matches previous KV slow-bleed case.
liam: monitoring graphs — resident pages per pod dropped ~18% on restarted pods, cluster-wide growth rate down from 3%/hr to 0.3%/hr. No new CUDA failures in last 8m.
ops-bot: autoscaler note: burst scaling triggered 2 new nodes at 22:20 UTC; capacity rebalanced.
juan: opened a bug/patch for allocator: reduce page size alignment and add periodic compaction hook. Link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/8421
maya: action items before handoff: 1) keep KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.65 and KVCACHE_EAGER_PRUNE=true for now, 2) keep prefetch disabled, 3) monitor OOMs/ CUDA errors for 1h, 4) coordinate CS message (Zoe), 5) prepare hotfix for allocator compaction.
liam: taking over oncall at 23:30 PST. I'll keep an eye on ACME-Pay route and node flaps. If growth resumes, I'll rollback warmup toggle and escalate to eng-runtime.
zoe-cs: prepping customer note: will send a status update indicating mitigations and ETA.
maya: current status at 22:28 UTC: stabilization in progress, no OOMs in last 12m on canary group, tail latency improved but still above baseline. Handoff to @liam.
liam: acknowledged. saving logs: `/archive/incidents/6791123587/` and adding runbook reference to incident ticket.
on-visible-note: full debug dump saved: `/var/logs/kv-dumps/6791123587-20260317.tar.gz`
maya: closing chat for now — escalate if anything flares. :thumbsup:
